content_text_body:
The level of commitment top leaders demonstrate towards diversity, inclusion, and belongingness practices speaks to the level of success these practices can have in any company. Persuading leadership to apply structural changes to include these practices requires high level of awareness, consistency, and accountability. 

### Support the need for diversity, inclusion, and belongingness practices with facts
Like with any change, you might experience resistance when building your case to gain support; nonetheless, share research data on the positive impact of these practices, analyze numbers on company demographics and compare it to data from similar companies, educate others on the negative consequences of ignoring these practices, and gain employee and manager support by increasing awareness on the matter. 

### Model inclusive leadership 
Adapting these practices is a journey where the final goal is to perpetuate a sense of diversity, inclusion, and belongingness as part of the organizational culture. Embrace authenticity in a work environment where employees feel safe and valued. Seek moments to gain feedback from employees on diversity, inclusion, and belongingness practices. Are they aware of them? Do they understand the purpose of these practices? Have they experienced bias against them? Share this feedback with your leadership and define measurable goals to transform the organizational culture. 

### Maintain open channels of communication 
Support the creation of focus groups (LGBTQ+, Latinx/Hispanic, Disability, etc.) and invite all employees to participate. These groups can inspire authenticity among your employees and lead them to have greater understanding and empathy about other groups.     

Read more about [how leadership can influence diversity and inclusion efforts](https://www.inc.com/katie-burke/5-ways-leadership-can-get-involved-in-diversity-inclusion.html).  

Remember you have an incredible potential to start and continue positive changes in your work environment.
